title: Part 6
content_zh: Du Fu's thatched cottage was blown apart by autumn winds. The roof flew over the river, children stole the scattered thatch, and rain soaked his bed. Yet in this moment of personal ruin, he wrote his greatest poem — a plea that the poor scholars of the world might all have shelter.
